Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play · School & learning

plot noun

of a play, a film or a story

also storyline, story line, the plot of the play, what happens in it, synopsis

classical

Ter. Ad. 22: argūmentum fābulae
Ter. And. 6: argūmentum narret
Liv. 7.2.8

argūmentum, argūmentī n.

noun, second declension

the plot, the story of a play or a poem

The comic poets’ word: the prologue tells the argūmentum. Its other common senses are a proof and a piece of evidence (see argument, evidence); Quintilian notes that it means the subject matter of any piece of writing (Quint. 5.10.9).

Other words

  • fābula, fābulae f. — the story

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Lewis & Short, s.v. fābula

    The story itself, or the play (see play); not the plot as distinct from the play.

Examples

  • Dehinc nē exspectētis argūmentum fābulae

    Next, don’t wait for the plot of the playTer. Ad. 22

  • Nōn ita dissimilī sunt argūmentō, sed tamen dissimilī ōrātiōne sunt factae ac stilō.

    Their plots are not so different, but they are written in a different language and style.Ter. And. 11–12

  • Līvius post aliquot annīs, quī ab saturīs ausus est prīmus argūmentō fābulam serere

    Livius, some years later, who was the first to leave the saturae and dare to weave a play out of a plotLiv. 7.2.8

See also play, story, argument, evidence, plot.
